affordance_in_statement: whenever two emitters u and v are linked by a conduit, the sum of their selected tuning frequencies (p_u + p_v) must not be a divisor of the sum of their squared frequencies (p_u^2 + p_v^2)
removal_suggestion: Replace the divisibility predicate with a genuinely nontrivial compatibility rule whose allowed pairs are not exactly the unequal frequency pairs; ideally make it depend on the conduit or endpoint data while preserving the stated sample behavior.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats every conduit as requiring different colors, thereby solving ordinary 3-coloring in vertex order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the divisibility condition together with the only available frequencies 1, 2, and 3

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the same proper-three-coloring constraint and backtracks over colors 1, 2, and 3.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the divisibility condition together with the only available frequencies 1, 2, and 3

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly reduces the arithmetic condition by checking all frequency pairs and concludes that equal frequencies are forbidden while unequal frequencies are allowed.

common_affordance: The arithmetic rule is exactly equivalent to requiring p_u != p_v on every conduit, so the problem is ordinary lexicographically smallest 3-coloring.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Enumerates all 3^n assignments with itertools.product instead of using constraint propagation or graph-coloring search, causing timeouts for n up to 40.

recommended_edit: Change the conduit safety predicate so that its valid and invalid frequency pairs are not simply unequal and equal, respectively; an endpoint- or conduit-dependent predicate would defeat all three surviving reductions at once.
